newsitem.title: CHINA: China insists on admission to WTO before Taiwan.
newsitem.headline: China insists on admission to WTO before Taiwan.

text.p: Beijing on Wednesday shrugged off a U.S. suggestion that Taiwan's accession to the World Trade Organisation (WTO) be independent of China's, insisting that it should gain entry first.
"We reiterate... our principle that China must join the WTO before Taiwan," said a spokesman for the Ministry of Foreign Trade and Economic Cooperation.

In Washington, U.S. Trade Representative Charlene Barshefsky said the United States believed Taiwan's accession to the WTO should be independent of China's and based on commercial, not political, criteria.

"Regarding WTO accession for Taiwan and the People's Republic of China, administration policy is that each accession will be judged on its own merits," Barshefsky said in a letter released to the media on Tuesday.
Asked to comment on the letter, the Chinese foreign trade ministry spokesman said: "We do not wish to see this happen. I think this will not happen."
China, which regards Taiwan as a renegade province, has said it would accept Taiwan's membership in the WTO as a customs territory -- but only after China itself is admitted.
Taiwan is said to be much closer to meeting WTO requirements than China, which is still trying to dismantle vestiges of a centrally planned economy.
At a WTO meeting in Geneva last Friday on Taiwan's accession, trade officials said Taipei's application seemed to be unavoidably linked to Beijing's.

China has been pushing to join the organisation on the easier terms of a developing country but some Western nations, including the United States, insist that its economy is too big for such treatment.
